content.text: I'll fetch the next page of five with the cursor to get ranks 6–10.
The cursor must be passed with the same `order_by` as the first page, so I'll repeat it.
Now I'll ask the store for the shortest path between Kestrel Farms (C-4) and Ostrava Machining (C-5), walking every relation in both directions.
The refusal says a `to` path must be projected as a graph, so I'll add `project: graph`.
To confirm Q9 in the store, I'll query products that have no order line (an `absent` step over `of_product`).
To check Q6 in the store, I'll aggregate line quantities by product category, joining each line to its order and excluding cancelled orders.
The aggregate projection takes `group_by` and `measures`, so I'll supply those instead.

I answered all nine questions from the store. Every read was pinned to position 74 of lake `trade`, so all answers describe the same state.

**1. Orders placed by Harbor Supplies (customer C-2)**
| Order | Date | Total | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| O-1002 | 2026-08-11 | 372.00 | shipped |
| O-1006 | 2026-09-09 | 142.50 | open |
| O-1011 | 2026-10-13 | 144.00 | cancelled |

Evidence: I listed all orders; these three have `customer = C-2`.

**2. Products on order O-1007**
- 2 units of Check valve DN25 (P-21), line L-1007-1
- 8 units of O-ring set (P-40), line L-1007-2

The prices fit: 2 × 42.50 + 8 × 12.00 = 181.00, which is the order's total.

**3. Suppliers of the products on order O-1004**
- Ball valve DN25 (P-20) is made by Lago Valvole (S-2), in Italy (IT).
- O-ring set (P-40) and Gasket DN25 (P-41) are made by Torino Guarnizioni (S-4), in Italy (IT).
- Hex bolt M8 (P-10) is made by Nordic Fasteners (S-1), in Sweden (SE).

**4. Open orders that contain a valve**
- **O-1004** has P-20 × 10.
- **O-1007** has P-21 × 2.
- **O-1009** has P-20 × 4.

O-1002 and O-1003 also contain valves, but both are shipped.

**5. Orders and totals per customer, all statuses** (from the store's own count and sum)
| Customer | Orders | Total |
|---|---|---|
| Delta Metals (C-1) | 3 | 1653.00 |
| Harbor Supplies (C-2) | 3 | 658.50 |
| Brightwater Utilities (C-3) | 2 | 2611.50 |
| Kestrel Farms (C-4) | 2 | 247.00 |
| Ostrava Machining (C-5) | 2 | 1035.00 |
| Vale Hardware (C-6) | 0 | 0.00 |

Vale Hardware doesn't appear in the store's grouped answer because it has no orders. The 12 orders total 6205.00.

**6. Units ordered per category, leaving out cancelled orders**
- fasteners: 4490 units (10 lines)
- seals: 163 units (5 lines)
- pumps: 14 units (5 lines)
- valves: 25 units (5 lines)

The two cancelled orders are left out: O-1005 (1 unit of P-30) and O-1011 (12 units of P-40). I checked each figure by hand against the lines.

**7. Order lines ranked 6 to 10 by quantity**
I read the ranking five lines at a time, sorted by quantity from highest, with the line id breaking ties.
| Rank | Line | Order | Product | Qty |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | L-1012-2 | O-1012 | P-12 | 300 |
| 7 | L-1006-2 | O-1006 | P-11 | 250 |
| 8 | L-1006-1 | O-1006 | P-10 | 200 |
| 9 | L-1004-4 | O-1004 | P-10 | 150 |
| 10 | L-1012-1 | O-1012 | P-10 | 90 |

The first page held ranks 1 to 5, ending with two lines of 400. Asking for the second page failed at first because I didn't repeat the sort order; it worked once I did.

**8. How Kestrel Farms and Ostrava Machining are connected**
The store's shortest-path query found a chain of six links:

Kestrel Farms (C-4) ← placed order O-1012 ← line L-1012-2 → Washer M8 (P-12) ← line L-1008-1 → order O-1008 → placed by Ostrava Machining (C-5)

In plain terms, both customers have ordered Washer M8: Kestrel Farms 300 units and Ostrava Machining 1200.

**9. Products never ordered**
- Threaded rod M8 (P-13, fasteners)
- Shaft seal 30mm (P-42, seals)

I asked the store for products that no order line points to; it returned only these two, which matches the full list of lines.
